messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: RStan size
parts:
As we are trying to make the source of RStan small, do we need to worry about the binary version size?
Now, if I run a R CMD check on the source, one note is 

* checking installed package size ... NOTE
 installed size is 230.0Mb
 sub-directories of 1Mb or more:
   include  109.4Mb
   libs      74.1Mb
   libstan   46.2Mb

Here libstan folder includes libstan.so, the shared version of libstan.a;
and libs includes rstan.so, the shared version of stanc, which would be loaded as RStan is loaded. 
(the include folder still include boost for now). 

On a side note, the above is compiled with g++.  When clang++ is used, the total size is even larger. 

Compared with the static versions, the above *.so's are really big.  
-rw-r--r-- 1 jq jq 3.1M Jul  6 21:37 libstan.a
-rw-r--r-- 1 jq jq 6.7M Jul  6 21:41 libstanc.a
-rwxr-xr-x 1 jq jq 2.3M Jul  6 21:41 stanc

--
Jiqiang

parts:
On Friday, July 6, 2012 11:07:03 PM UTC-4, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
As we are trying to make the source of RStan small, do we need to worry about the binary version size?
Yes, although I don't know if there are any hard and fast rules about the installed size.

Now, if I run a R CMD check on the source, one note is 

* checking installed package size ... NOTE
 installed size is 230.0Mb
 sub-directories of 1Mb or more:
   include  109.4Mb
   libs      74.1Mb
   libstan   46.2Mb

include/ should ultimately be empty, once we rely on the RcppEigen package and the system Boost.

But that is still a lot bigger than any other R package I have installed

goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/usr/lib/R/site-library$ du -h -d 1 | sort -h | tail
3.3M    ./rgl
3.7M    ./fPortfolio
4.1M    ./Rcmdr
5.0M    ./VGAM
5.6M    ./qtl
9.5M    ./GenABEL
11M     ./Rcpp
18M     ./RGtk2
33M     ./mapdata
195M    .

You can cut RStan down a little bit more by excluding src/test/ and logos/. Also, it seems that make clean-all does not eliminate the .o files in the subdirectories of src/ so that adds to the size. Even still, CRAN is probably not going to be too happy.

 Ben

We want to step back from -O3 only as a last
resort. It's about 10 times faster than -O0;
how the -O1 or -O2 behave differs between clang++
and g++. The upside is that it's faster to compile
with less optimization.

Right.
> -- Include the -s flag
What does this do?

> P.S. Unrelated thing, but it would be better to write the *.csv files to tempdir() rather than getwd() because the
> working directory might not be writable by the user. But the *.csv files will get deleted when the user closes R, so we
> would need to direct the user to copy them elsewhere if desired.

Could we do this

1. if user supplies file name, use that if it's writable, if
not bomb and say it's not writable.

2. if user does not supply a file name, use getwd() if it's
writable.

3. as a last resort, use tempdir() and issue a warning

I don't know how easy it is to test file properties in R.

- Bob

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: RStan size
parts:
Finally, I managed to build rstan.so and libstan.so using -Os -s by adding a Makefile in src though Makefile is not encouraged due to it might be less portable. 

It is not trivial to have a package defined CXXFLAGS (and other flags) as what is essentially done in R is 

make -f 'Makevars' -f '/usr/lib/R/etc/Makeconf' -f '/usr/share/R/share/make/shlib.mk' -f '/home/jq/.R/Makevars' SHLIB_LDFLAGS='$(SHLIB_CXXLDFLAGS)' SHLIB_LD='$(SHLIB_CXXLD)' SHLIB='rstan.so'

The first Makevars is the package supplied src/Makevars.  So whatever I do regarding CXXFLAGS in src/Makevars would be overridden later. 

But for src/Makefile, R does

make -f '/usr/lib/R/etc/Makeconf' -f 'Makefile' -f '/home/jq/.R/Makevars'

--
Jiqiang

On Saturday, July 7, 2012 1:31:36 PM UTC-4, Ben Goodrich wrote:

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] RStan size & compiler options
parts:
On Mon, Jul 9, 2012 at 3:22 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
If I understood the previous exchange correctly, your plan is to
use -Os and -s for the RStan builds by default and let
users modify HOME/.R/Makevars if they want to build a fast
version of Stan?

I guess there is no plan yet.  It is that just CRAN is too picky.  Even what I did not is 
not encouraged as the doc says O3 or O2 might not be options for other C++ compilers. 
If O3 is workable, I am happy to use that (the main problem might be the -g options which 
is the default options in my installed R.)  But I have not built the package under different 
options to see what size we end up with.  And actually what works for me now might only 
work on Linux.  On different platforms, R might treat those Makevar and Makefile differently,
which I am not sure and I do not think it is well documented.  At least I know I still 
could not make RStan work on Windows after some efforts. 

In addition, we might be able to build libstan under O3.  But when compiling the models, 
the options are up to the user's R configuration.
Do you know how much slower -Os -s is than -O3?
Not tested yet.

Given Andrew's concerns for speed, I don't think we're going
to want to release something that's significantly slower than
-O3.

In my tests, I found -O0 to be about 1/10 as fast as -O3.

- Bob
